# **CFTC and ETF Report** _A weekly update of futures and exchange traded fund activity._ • Precious metal prices were weak over the end of December, falling particularly heavily as the Euro fell against the US Dollar on the 28th. The prices of all four metals bounced fairly convincingly to end the year back where they had been before Christmas. However, since the start of 2012, continued worries over the Euro have led to a spell of Dollar strength which has been negative for commodity prices. Gold and silver have outperformed, suggesting some safe haven bid exists. Platinum is currently trading close to where it started the year while palladium has lost ground. We expect the Euro to come under continued pressure for the next few weeks at least, suggesting that the prices of the three white metals may remain under some pressure. • Net long speculative positioning on the futures exchanges remains low for all four of the major precious metals. Over the end of 2011 and the start of 2012, silver saw the most positive investor interest as positions moved back over 100 million ounces. Global interest in platinum changed little while investors reduced their long exposure to both gold and palladium. Gold and silver face further selling this week due to index rebalancing. • The first week of 2012 saw precious metal ETF investors in bearish mood. The only metal to see increases in its global holdings was platinum. Gold, silver and palladium all saw net selling. **David Jollie david.jollie@mitprecious.com Tel: +44 20 7489 6767** **09 January 2012** ##### **New York:** 200 Park Avenue, New York, NY 10166 0130 Tel: +1 212 878 4122 ##### **London:** 4th Floor, St Martins Court, 10 Paternoster Row, London EC4M 7BB Tel: +44 20 7489 6767 ##### **Hong Kong:** Suite 1306, Two Exchange Square, 8 Connaught Place, Central, Hong Kong Tel: +852 2899 2026 ##### **Tokyo:** 2-1 Ohtemachi 1-Chome, Chiyoda-Ku, Tokyo 100 Tel: +81 33 285 3407 ##### **Singapore:** 80 Robinson Road, #15-02, Singapore, 068898 Tel: +65 6372 8050 **Mitsui Global Precious Metals | CFTC and ETF Weekly Report** **09 January 2012** ### **Gold CFTC data to 3 January 2012; ETF data to 6 January 2012.** #### **Exchange (COMEX and TOCOM) and ETF Gold Investment (oz)** ||**COMEX**

Foreign exchange movements accounted for most of the bigger movements: the Dollar strengthened against the Euro on the 28th and gold fell to a low of $1,530 before recovering. On the 3rd, the Euro weakened in an early bout of false optimism and gold climbed back over $1,600. Since then, the Euro has fallen back sharply but gold has firmed a little, adding another $10 with support from strong Chinese buying and a sense of bullishness in the wider investor community. - On the futures markets, gold saw selling both in Tokyo and in New York. Net long speculative positions on TOCOM fell by 70,000 ounces to 1.29 million ounces while NYMEX positions declined from 17.0 to 16.8 million ounces. Positioning is now rather low and, with index rebalancing due to take place this week, we expect to see some further selling pressure in the days to come. Any subsequent increase in investor interest could help drive higher prices. - Global Exchange Traded Fund gold holdings fell for the fourth successive week to the 6th of January, dropping 334,000 ounces to 68.9 million ounces. Unusually, the main change was selling from the Swiss ZKB fund with little action seen in the other gold ETFs. #### **Gold Exchange Investment, April 09—Jan 12** 40 2,000 Gold price, $/oz

- Despite lacklustre physical demand, silver started 2012 relatively positively in price terms. On the 28th of December, it fell sharply lower as the Euro slumped against the Dollar again. It lurched from $28.70 to a short-lived low of $26.40 on the 29th before shooting back higher to end the year at $27.90. The recent flirtation with the $30 level continued in early January as the Euro firmed and silver moved up to $29.70 on the 3rd. The realisation that the Euro problems will not be solved, or even fully addressed, for some time to come weakened the Euro in the following days, however, and silver slipped back closer to the $29 level. - Silver investors started 2011 in slightly bullish mood. Open interest on COMEX increased as long contracts held by larger investors climbed by more than ten per cent. Net long speculative interest climbed by 9.9 million ounces to 102.6 million ounces but remains low. As in the gold market, index rebalancing should apply some downwards pressure to the silver price in the coming days. - As with gold, silver saw ETF selling for the fourth successive week leading up to the 6th of January. Although buying was seen in some funds, the more widespread trend was one of net selling, with most of the funds we monitor reporting net outflows of metal. - The platinum price looked weak coming into the end of 2012 and, although it is currently trading just above $1,400, at close to the level where it started the year, this negative trend seems to be continuing. Following Christmas, platinum traded at $1,430 before a slump in the Euro sent it plummeting to a low of just under $1,350. This was in thin trading though and could not be sustained, with platinum recovering to $1,400 at the end of the year and $1,430 on the 3rd as the Euro surprisingly firmed. Since then, further Dollar strength has weighed upon the price despite strong buying interest from Chinese consumers. Platinum is currently trading just above $1,400, over $215 per ounce below gold. - Globally, there was little change in platinum futures interest in the week to the 3rd of January. What TOCOM investors sold was balanced by additional buying interest from NYMEX investors. Combined net long speculative positions declined by 11,000 ounces to 1.2 million ounces. NYMEX activity seemed to show a gentle bullishness from investors there with short covering following the previous week’s rapid rebound from the postChristmas lows in the platinum price. - In the first week of 2012, there was a small amount of buying in the platinum Exchange Traded Funds, a slightly positive sign of investor attitudes. 3,400 ounces more platinum were bought than were sold, with US investors the main buyers. 4 **Mitsui Global Precious Me

- Having performed strongly in price terms in December, palladium ran out of energy in early January. While the other precious metals crashed lower on the 28th under pressure from the foreign exchange markets, palladium was remarkably robust, falling only from $660 to a low of $630. By the end of the year, it had recovered to $650 and palladium pushed on to a high of $669 on the 3rd as the Euro strengthened on an early burst of economic optimism. This proved to be misplaced as the Dollar firmed in the following days, driving palladium back to a low for the year so far of $610. It is currently trading at $617. - For palladium, investor activity on the futures exchanges was remarkably negative with NYMEX positions falling by nine per cent to 534,000 ounces. Open interest was little changed so this was driven by a mix of long liquidation and rising short positions. While we expect to see higher palladium prices this year, last week’s price decline will have tested investors’ appetite and set a negative tone to start the year. - Further ETF selling placed some downward pressure on the palladium price in the first week of 2012. 12,800 ounces of metal were sold, marking the ninth successive week in which investors sold more palladium than they bought. Holdings now stand at 1.72 mil
